questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that the University was in a big city (it is really one hour by bus from the citycenter buuut), but had mountains to hike and ski in within one hour of driving.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: They had two zoom meeting for incoming exchange student. I did not go to them, but i guess theu could have been helpfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I stayed in a 6 person apartment. It was also possible to get studios by your self og to live in houses or smaller aparments.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
You could by meal plans. 

All housing had kitchens, but there is no culture for sharing the utilities, so most exchange students have to buy all the kitchen utilities when they arrive. I hope UBC are working on a better soultion.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Campus housing can be really close to all the facilities on campus, which is a big big plus. Don't expect to find your new best friends in your apartment. Most people are 18 or 19 and there is not really a culture for having a social life with your roomates. ,People have to change housing every year.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was super easy. You just get your key and sign a short form and that is it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get there, you sign a paper, you get the key, you send in pictures of your room.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I didn't get any.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get them at first, but wrote to the professors and got all the courses i wanted (I changed 3 courses) during the period, where you can change courses. It is super easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't panic. Everything is so much easier when you are at the destination. Talk to the professors.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was honestly too easy.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
International Macroeconioms and Finance was quite difficult and the pace high. Michael expects you to follow his pace. 

The other courses are way easier than the courses at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures are smaller and there is more interaction than the lectures at KU. They also have discussion classes, but don't use them as much as at KU. The assignments, participation and the mid-term exam all counts to your grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Macroeconomics and Finance (International Economics)
Quantative Economics Modelling with Data Sciece applied (økonomisk valgfag)
Introduction to Game Theory and Applications (micro 3)
Market structure (industrial organization)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
International Macroeconomics and Finance - if you want to learn a lot (but it is also one of the more difficult courses, where you have to study)
Quantative Economics Modelling with Data Sciece applied  - if you want to learn python and do a minimum and still pass withour problems. 
Introduction to Game Theory and Applications - Jonathan Graves, the professor, is amazing. Probably the best teacher I ever had. 
Market structure (industrial organization) - easy.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of great places to do sports. (Badminton, Swimming, weight lifting)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it was a bit limited because of covid 19.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the outdoor club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the nature. Go skiing, go hiking, go to the beach.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs. Talk to your class mates. Don't expect to get too many local friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you go in the spring, you have to buy your season ski pass before december, as they stop selling them and one day passes are SO expensive. 

Get out in the nature from the first weekend. 

Don't spend to much time studiyng. Have fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nope.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: None really.
